erase_forecast.basis: scenario has no OCP HBF physical memory component

assumptions: Unsampled layers take their class's sampled step: the DRAM row openings that differ between same-class layers because their buffer addresses straddle row boundaries differently are assumed negligible and are not bounded; representative-point full native runs check every unsampled layer against its class interval.

The samples run on one settled KV block layout, the block tables a long stationary refill run reaches; the DRAM row openings and NAND bank loads that change as the batch's tables change between steps are assumed negligible and are not bounded.
Native serving, planner, GPU cost profiles and physical DRAM/NAND/SRAM services; no paper_* execution.
Paper Table I per-GPU capacity and interface budgets, BF16 model and KV, decimal workload K.

Native NAND page service with OCP HBF v0.7 control and Table I geometry and timing; the host owns KV placement and block opens and there is no FTL or GC. Block size and erase time are research assumptions; every plane erasing at once is not stated by OCP.

NAND-backed KV: the host starts an import as a slot frees, fixes the step it joins and picks the free block that keeps its tail off the other tails' banks, knowing no request's length; reads and writes follow the block's address. The pick costs no time. Blocks mix requests of unequal lifetimes in real use, which holds extra NAND but moves no data.
8x40MB intermediate SRAM is modeled as a 320MB pool split across 128 die-local channel ports; aggregate bandwidth/latency/credits are explicit research inputs.
External Prefill producer source uses native DDR5 service geometry expanded to at least world x 100 GB/s; PD links and target KV writes remain the intended bottlenecks (research assumption).

PD import (user approved 2026-10-24): one stream per target rank, all streams concurrent; each import owns a 64 MiB source buffer cut into 1 MiB chunk slots dealt round-robin to its streams; a chunk holds its slot from source read until its target write completes (RDMA source-buffer semantics), so a stream keeps at most its slot count in flight while adjacent chunks' reads, links and writes overlap on the native timelines.
External producer streams prompt-1 KV tokens; native one-token final-prompt generates the first visible output and pays its complete cost.
Warmup seeds use real age-extended prompt histories and shorter remaining outputs to stagger completion; fresh measured requests retain the declared paper lengths.

Warmup-seed KV is preloaded with allocator pages and capacity charged but no paid import; controllers start clean with no in-flight writes (the paper does not publish its initial state). Every fresh request pays its native PD import.

Continuous batching: freed slots refill at the next step from the pre-imported requests of their own EP group (1 group(s), up to 2 per group, 2 in total; pool sized from the slots a group frees per step and the steps one import spans at Table I write rates, x4 margin; its KV counts against capacity); final-prompt queries join mixed decode cohorts.

Native layer runs on independent copies of the first continuous-refill boundary are physical; the stationary step, PD-import extra, refill schedule, cohorts and visible Tokens are separate conditional predictions.

Unsampled layers take their class's sampled step: the DRAM row openings that differ between same-class layers because their buffer addresses straddle row boundaries differently are assumed negligible and are not bounded; representative-point full native runs check every unsampled layer against its class interval.
Each point's independent error budget retains the 10% target; conditional budgets are not full-window detailed validation or silicon/paper accuracy guarantees.

settings.native_layouts: legal DP/TP/PP/EP and pipeline microbatch layouts
settings.interpolation: linear TPOT upper bound between the adjacent measured points bracketing the SLO
settings.acceptance: one fast native run at the interpolated batch of the best layout and of every layout predicted within acceptance_margin of it; one above the SLO joins the bracket and the batch is interpolated again, settling at the bracket's passing end within a step of a measured batch; one that proves too big bisects under it; falls back to the best measured passing point
settings.no_rising_line: double the largest point below the SLO, or halve the smallest above it
settings.beyond_native_reach: largest measured point, marked limited, never extrapolated
settings.capacity: bypass KV capacity until a native point reaches it, then native capacity rejections; a KV rejection's reported native capacity batch is measured next
settings.import_speed: native_stationary_refill_not_always_ready is a too-big point; halving/bisection is reused and the limit is native_import_limited
settings.interval_width: native_stationary_independent_budget_exceeded is a too-big point; halving/bisection is reused and the limit is native_interval_limited
settings.too_big: a target at or past the smallest too-big batch bisects from the largest passing point below it, after any reported native capacity below that batch has been tried
settings.wall_projection: measured wall without the Prefill pass, as measured, against the candidate wall budget; no concurrency divisor
settings.wall_budget: 6 h per candidate and Prefill pass, a guard against a hung worker that must not decide a result: a budget change reuses saved rows, and a row killed under a smaller budget runs again
settings.stopping: SLO upper-bound bracket; physical capacity, memory and wall limits remain hard limits
settings.pruning: branch and bound in bypass rate-bound order: the anchor searches from its default first point; later layouts first run where passing the SLO matches the anchor's best passing rate and are pruned when the bypass rate bound (below any native limit, divided by bypass_tpot_floor) or a point above the SLO (rate x (1 + rate_margin)) falls below the case's best measured passing rate, or when a point below the SLO cannot reach it with TPOT growing at slope_floor x min(1, the case's least native/bypass slope ratio from a point within the SLO) x the bypass slope
settings.max_batch: paper Fig. 3: after the throughput search, the largest per-GPU batch within the SLO by the same branch and bound per layout (bypass batch bound with bypass_tpot_floor, a point above the SLO times 1 + rate_margin, the slope floor), one acceptance run at the best layout's interpolated batch, falling back to the largest measured passing point

The samples run on one settled KV block layout, the block tables a long stationary refill run reaches; the DRAM row openings and NAND bank loads that change as the batch's tables change between steps are assumed negligible and are not bounded.

progress.wall_breakdown_scope: exclusive wall intervals between native progress stage transitions; not simulated hardware latency

cases.selection_scope: highest conditionally accepted projected per-GPU throughput among the sampled (DP, TP, PP, EP) layout and per-replica batch candidates; not a global optimum or maximum feasible batch

settings.native_layouts: legal DP/TP/PP/EP and pipeline microbatch layouts
settings.interpolation: linear TPOT upper bound between the adjacent measured points bracketing the SLO
settings.acceptance: one fast native run at the interpolated batch of the best layout and of every layout predicted within acceptance_margin of it; one above the SLO joins the bracket and the batch is interpolated again, settling at the bracket's passing end within a step of a measured batch; one that proves too big bisects under it; falls back to the best measured passing point
settings.no_rising_line: double the largest point below the SLO, or halve the smallest above it
settings.beyond_native_reach: largest measured point, marked limited, never extrapolated
settings.capacity: bypass KV capacity until a native point reaches it, then native capacity rejections; a KV rejection's reported native capacity batch is measured next
settings.import_speed: native_stationary_refill_not_always_ready is a too-big point; halving/bisection is reused and the limit is native_import_limited
settings.interval_width: native_stationary_independent_budget_exceeded is a too-big point; halving/bisection is reused and the limit is native_interval_limited
settings.too_big: a target at or past the smallest too-big batch bisects from the largest passing point below it, after any reported native capacity below that batch has been tried
settings.wall_projection: measured wall without the Prefill pass, as measured, against the candidate wall budget; no concurrency divisor
settings.wall_budget: 6 h per candidate and Prefill pass, a guard against a hung worker that must not decide a result: a budget change reuses saved rows, and a row killed under a smaller budget runs again
settings.stopping: SLO upper-bound bracket; physical capacity, memory and wall limits remain hard limits
settings.pruning: branch and bound in bypass rate-bound order: the anchor searches from its default first point; later layouts first run where passing the SLO matches the anchor's best passing rate and are pruned when the bypass rate bound (below any native limit, divided by bypass_tpot_floor) or a point above the SLO (rate x (1 + rate_margin)) falls below the case's best measured passing rate, or when a point below the SLO cannot reach it with TPOT growing at slope_floor x min(1, the case's least native/bypass slope ratio from a point within the SLO) x the bypass slope
settings.max_batch: paper Fig. 3: after the throughput search, the largest per-GPU batch within the SLO by the same branch and bound per layout (bypass batch bound with bypass_tpot_floor, a point above the SLO times 1 + rate_margin, the slope floor), one acceptance run at the best layout's interpolated batch, falling back to the largest measured passing point

assumptions: Unsampled layers take their class's sampled step: the DRAM row openings that differ between same-class layers because their buffer addresses straddle row boundaries differently are assumed negligible and are not bounded; representative-point full native runs check every unsampled layer against its class interval.

Native serving, planner, GPU cost profiles and physical DRAM/NAND/SRAM services; no paper_* execution.
Paper Table I per-GPU capacity and interface budgets, BF16 model and KV, decimal workload K.

Native NAND page service with OCP HBF v0.7 control and Table I geometry and timing; the host owns KV placement and block opens and there is no FTL or GC. Block size and erase time are research assumptions; every plane erasing at once is not stated by OCP.

NAND-backed KV: the host starts an import as a slot frees, fixes the step it joins and picks the free block that keeps its tail off the other tails' banks, knowing no request's length; reads and writes follow the block's address. The pick costs no time. Blocks mix requests of unequal lifetimes in real use, which holds extra NAND but moves no data.
8x40MB intermediate SRAM is modeled as a 320MB pool split across 128 die-local channel ports; aggregate bandwidth/latency/credits are explicit research inputs.
External Prefill producer source uses native DDR5 service geometry expanded to at least world x 100 GB/s; PD links and target KV writes remain the intended bottlenecks (research assumption).

PD import (user approved 2026-10-24): one stream per target rank, all streams concurrent; each import owns a 64 MiB source buffer cut into 1 MiB chunk slots dealt round-robin to its streams; a chunk holds its slot from source read until its target write completes (RDMA source-buffer semantics), so a stream keeps at most its slot count in flight while adjacent chunks' reads, links and writes overlap on the native timelines.
External producer streams prompt-1 KV tokens; native one-token final-prompt generates the first visible output and pays its complete cost.
Warmup seeds use real age-extended prompt histories and shorter remaining outputs to stagger completion; fresh measured requests retain the declared paper lengths.

Warmup-seed KV is preloaded with allocator pages and capacity charged but no paid import; controllers start clean with no in-flight writes (the paper does not publish its initial state). Every fresh request pays its native PD import.

Continuous batching: freed slots refill at the next step from the pre-imported requests of their own EP group (1 group(s), up to 4 per group, 4 in total; pool sized from the slots a group frees per step and the steps one import spans at Table I write rates, x4 margin; its KV counts against capacity); final-prompt queries join mixed decode cohorts.

Native layer runs on independent copies of the first continuous-refill boundary are physical; the stationary step, PD-import extra, refill schedule, cohorts and visible Tokens are separate conditional predictions.

Unsampled layers take their class's sampled step: the DRAM row openings that differ between same-class layers because their buffer addresses straddle row boundaries differently are assumed negligible and are not bounded; representative-point full native runs check every unsampled layer against its class interval.
Each point's independent error budget retains the 10% target; conditional budgets are not full-window detailed validation or silicon/paper accuracy guarantees.

replica_scaling.scope: native_window_forecast and approximation hold the single simulated replica; metrics and metric intervals below are scaled to the cluster

settings.acceptance: one fast native run at the interpolated batch of the best layout and of every layout predicted within acceptance_margin of it; one above the SLO joins the bracket and the batch is interpolated again, settling at the bracket's passing end within a step of a measured batch; one that proves too big bisects under it; falls back to the best measured passing point
settings.no_rising_line: double the largest point below the SLO, or halve the smallest above it
settings.beyond_native_reach: largest measured point, marked limited, never extrapolated
settings.capacity: bypass KV capacity until a native point reaches it, then native capacity rejections; a KV rejection's reported native capacity batch is measured next
settings.import_speed: native_stationary_refill_not_always_ready is a too-big point; halving/bisection is reused and the limit is native_import_limited
settings.interval_width: native_stationary_independent_budget_exceeded is a too-big point; halving/bisection is reused and the limit is native_interval_limited
settings.too_big: a target at or past the smallest too-big batch bisects from the largest passing point below it, after any reported native capacity below that batch has been tried
settings.wall_projection: measured wall without the Prefill pass, as measured, against the candidate wall budget; no concurrency divisor
settings.wall_budget: 6 h per candidate and Prefill pass, a guard against a hung worker that must not decide a result: a budget change reuses saved rows, and a row killed under a smaller budget runs again
settings.stopping: SLO upper-bound bracket; physical capacity, memory and wall limits remain hard limits
settings.pruning: branch and bound in bypass rate-bound order: the anchor searches from its default first point; later layouts first run where passing the SLO matches the anchor's best passing rate and are pruned when the bypass rate bound (below any native limit, divided by bypass_tpot_floor) or a point above the SLO (rate x (1 + rate_margin)) falls below the case's best measured passing rate, or when a point below the SLO cannot reach it with TPOT growing at slope_floor x min(1, the case's least native/bypass slope ratio from a point within the SLO) x the bypass slope
settings.max_batch: paper Fig. 3: after the throughput search, the largest per-GPU batch within the SLO by the same branch and bound per layout (bypass batch bound with bypass_tpot_floor, a point above the SLO times 1 + rate_margin, the slope floor), one acceptance run at the best layout's interpolated batch, falling back to the largest measured passing point

erase_forecast.basis: calibration+holdout per-channel host/scratchpad writes scaled to all model layers; the fastest channel clocks batches; each batch erases one unified block per due die and all HBF components are charged as one visible erase

assumptions: Unsampled layers take their class's sampled step: the DRAM row openings that differ between same-class layers because their buffer addresses straddle row boundaries differently are assumed negligible and are not bounded; representative-point full native runs check every unsampled layer against its class interval.

Native serving, planner, GPU cost profiles and physical DRAM/NAND/SRAM services; no paper_* execution.
Paper Table I per-GPU capacity and interface budgets, BF16 model and KV, decimal workload K.

Native NAND page service with OCP HBF v0.7 control and Table I geometry and timing; the host owns KV placement and block opens and there is no FTL or GC. Block size and erase time are research assumptions; every plane erasing at once is not stated by OCP.

NAND-backed KV: the host starts an import as a slot frees, fixes the step it joins and picks the free block that keeps its tail off the other tails' banks, knowing no request's length; reads and writes follow the block's address. The pick costs no time. Blocks mix requests of unequal lifetimes in real use, which holds extra NAND but moves no data.
8x40MB intermediate SRAM is modeled as a 320MB pool split across 128 die-local channel ports; aggregate bandwidth/latency/credits are explicit research inputs.
External Prefill producer source uses native DDR5 service geometry expanded to at least world x 100 GB/s; PD links and target KV writes remain the intended bottlenecks (research assumption).

PD import (user approved 2026-10-24): one stream per target rank, all streams concurrent; each import owns a 64 MiB source buffer cut into 1 MiB chunk slots dealt round-robin to its streams; a chunk holds its slot from source read until its target write completes (RDMA source-buffer semantics), so a stream keeps at most its slot count in flight while adjacent chunks' reads, links and writes overlap on the native timelines.
External producer streams prompt-1 KV tokens; native one-token final-prompt generates the first visible output and pays its complete cost.
Warmup seeds use real age-extended prompt histories and shorter remaining outputs to stagger completion; fresh measured requests retain the declared paper lengths.

Warmup-seed KV is preloaded with allocator pages and capacity charged but no paid import; controllers start clean with no in-flight writes (the paper does not publish its initial state). Every fresh request pays its native PD import.

Continuous batching: freed slots refill at the next step from the pre-imported requests of their own EP group (8 group(s), up to 4 per group, 32 in total; pool sized from the slots a group frees per step and the steps one import spans at Table I write rates, x4 margin; its KV counts against capacity); final-prompt queries join mixed decode cohorts.

Attention data parallelism over 8 EP groups: each group owns B/ep requests and runs their attention, dense MLP, router and shared expert on its own TP ranks (dense weights replicated per group, KV only on the owner group); MoE experts are shared by native all_to_all dispatch and combine across groups, and every layer ends at one cross-group barrier.

Native layer runs on independent copies of the first continuous-refill boundary are physical; the stationary step, PD-import extra, refill schedule, cohorts and visible Tokens are separate conditional predictions.

Unsampled layers take their class's sampled step: the DRAM row openings that differ between same-class layers because their buffer addresses straddle row boundaries differently are assumed negligible and are not bounded; representative-point full native runs check every unsampled layer against its class interval.
Each point's independent error budget retains the 10% target; conditional budgets are not full-window detailed validation or silicon/paper accuracy guarantees.

assumptions: Native serving, planner, GPU cost profiles and physical DRAM/NAND/SRAM services; no paper_* execution.
Paper Table I per-GPU capacity and interface budgets, BF16 model and KV, decimal workload K.

Native NAND page service with OCP HBF v0.7 control and Table I geometry and timing; the host owns KV placement and block opens and there is no FTL or GC. Block size and erase time are research assumptions; every plane erasing at once is not stated by OCP.

NAND-backed KV: the host starts an import as a slot frees, fixes the step it joins and picks the free block that keeps its tail off the other tails' banks, knowing no request's length; reads and writes follow the block's address. The pick costs no time. Blocks mix requests of unequal lifetimes in real use, which holds extra NAND but moves no data.
8x40MB intermediate SRAM is modeled as a 320MB pool split across 128 die-local channel ports; aggregate bandwidth/latency/credits are explicit research inputs.
External Prefill producer source uses native DDR5 service geometry expanded to at least world x 100 GB/s; PD links and target KV writes remain the intended bottlenecks (research assumption).

PD import (user approved 2026-10-24): one stream per target rank, all streams concurrent; each import owns a 64 MiB source buffer cut into 1 MiB chunk slots dealt round-robin to its streams; a chunk holds its slot from source read until its target write completes (RDMA source-buffer semantics), so a stream keeps at most its slot count in flight while adjacent chunks' reads, links and writes overlap on the native timelines.
External producer streams prompt-1 KV tokens; native one-token final-prompt generates the first visible output and pays its complete cost.
Warmup seeds use real age-extended prompt histories and shorter remaining outputs to stagger completion; fresh measured requests retain the declared paper lengths.

Warmup-seed KV is preloaded with allocator pages and capacity charged but no paid import; controllers start clean with no in-flight writes (the paper does not publish its initial state). Every fresh request pays its native PD import.

Continuous batching: freed slots refill at the next step from the pre-imported requests of their own EP group (1 group(s), up to 8 per group, 8 in total; pool sized from the slots a group frees per step and the steps one import spans at Table I write rates, x4 margin; its KV counts against capacity); final-prompt queries join mixed decode cohorts.

Native layer runs on independent copies of the first continuous-refill boundary are physical; the stationary step, PD-import extra, refill schedule, cohorts and visible Tokens are separate conditional predictions.

Unsampled layers take their class's sampled step: the DRAM row openings that differ between same-class layers because their buffer addresses straddle row boundaries differently are assumed negligible and are not bounded; representative-point full native runs check every unsampled layer against its class interval.
Each point's independent error budget retains the 10% target; conditional budgets are not full-window detailed validation or silicon/paper accuracy guarantees.

NAND-backed KV: the host starts an import as a slot frees, fixes the step it joins and picks the free block that keeps its tail off the other tails' banks, knowing no request's length; reads and writes follow the block's address. The pick costs no time. Blocks mix requests of unequal lifetimes in real use, which holds extra NAND but moves no data.
8x40MB intermediate SRAM is modeled as a 320MB pool split across 128 die-local channel ports; aggregate bandwidth/latency/credits are explicit research inputs.
External Prefill producer source uses native DDR5 service geometry expanded to at least world x 100 GB/s; PD links and target KV writes remain the intended bottlenecks (research assumption).

PD import (user approved 2026-10-24): one stream per target rank, all streams concurrent; each import owns a 64 MiB source buffer cut into 1 MiB chunk slots dealt round-robin to its streams; a chunk holds its slot from source read until its target write completes (RDMA source-buffer semantics), so a stream keeps at most its slot count in flight while adjacent chunks' reads, links and writes overlap on the native timelines.
External producer streams prompt-1 KV tokens; native one-token final-prompt generates the first visible output and pays its complete cost.

Continuous batching: freed slots refill at the next step from the pre-imported requests of their own EP group (1 group(s), up to 4 per group, 4 in total; pool sized from the slots a group frees per step and the steps one import spans at Table I write rates, x4 margin; its KV counts against capacity); final-prompt queries join mixed decode cohorts.

Native NAND page service with OCP HBF v0.7 control and Table I geometry and timing; the host owns KV placement and block opens and there is no FTL or GC. Block size and erase time are research assumptions; every plane erasing at once is not stated by OCP.

NAND-backed KV: the host starts an import as a slot frees, fixes the step it joins and picks the free block that keeps its tail off the other tails' banks, knowing no request's length; reads and writes follow the block's address. The pick costs no time. Blocks mix requests of unequal lifetimes in real use, which holds extra NAND but moves no data.
8x40MB intermediate SRAM is modeled as a 320MB pool split across 128 die-local channel ports; aggregate bandwidth/latency/credits are explicit research inputs.
External Prefill producer source uses native DDR5 service geometry expanded to at least world x 100 GB/s; PD links and target KV writes remain the intended bottlenecks (research assumption).

PD import (user approved 2026-10-24): one stream per target rank, all streams concurrent; each import owns a 64 MiB source buffer cut into 1 MiB chunk slots dealt round-robin to its streams; a chunk holds its slot from source read until its target write completes (RDMA source-buffer semantics), so a stream keeps at most its slot count in flight while adjacent chunks' reads, links and writes overlap on the native timelines.
External producer streams prompt-1 KV tokens; native one-token final-prompt generates the first visible output and pays its complete cost.
Warmup seeds use real age-extended prompt histories and shorter remaining outputs to stagger completion; fresh measured requests retain the declared paper lengths.

Warmup-seed KV is preloaded with allocator pages and capacity charged but no paid import; controllers start clean with no in-flight writes (the paper does not publish its initial state). Every fresh request pays its native PD import.

Continuous batching: freed slots refill at the next step from the pre-imported requests of their own EP group (1 group(s), up to 2 per group, 2 in total; pool sized from the slots a group frees per step and the steps one import spans at Table I write rates, x4 margin; its KV counts against capacity); final-prompt queries join mixed decode cohorts.

Native layer runs on independent copies of the first continuous-refill boundary are physical; the stationary step, PD-import extra, refill schedule, cohorts and visible Tokens are separate conditional predictions.

Unsampled layers take their class's sampled step: the DRAM row openings that differ between same-class layers because their buffer addresses straddle row boundaries differently are assumed negligible and are not bounded; representative-point full native runs check every unsampled layer against its class interval.
Each point's independent error budget retains the 10% target; conditional budgets are not full-window detailed validation or silicon/paper accuracy guarantees.

Paper Table I per-GPU capacity and interface budgets, BF16 model and KV, decimal workload K.

Native NAND page service with OCP HBF v0.7 control and Table I geometry and timing; the host owns KV placement and block opens and there is no FTL or GC. Block size and erase time are research assumptions; every plane erasing at once is not stated by OCP.

NAND-backed KV: the host starts an import as a slot frees, fixes the step it joins and picks the free block that keeps its tail off the other tails' banks, knowing no request's length; reads and writes follow the block's address. The pick costs no time. Blocks mix requests of unequal lifetimes in real use, which holds extra NAND but moves no data.
8x40MB intermediate SRAM is modeled as a 320MB pool split across 128 die-local channel ports; aggregate bandwidth/latency/credits are explicit research inputs.
External Prefill producer source uses native DDR5 service geometry expanded to at least world x 100 GB/s; PD links and target KV writes remain the intended bottlenecks (research assumption).

PD import (user approved 2026-10-24): one stream per target rank, all streams concurrent; each import owns a 64 MiB source buffer cut into 1 MiB chunk slots dealt round-robin to its streams; a chunk holds its slot from source read until its target write completes (RDMA source-buffer semantics), so a stream keeps at most its slot count in flight while adjacent chunks' reads, links and writes overlap on the native timelines.
External producer streams prompt-1 KV tokens; native one-token final-prompt generates the first visible output and pays its complete cost.
Warmup seeds use real age-extended prompt histories and shorter remaining outputs to stagger completion; fresh measured requests retain the declared paper lengths.

Warmup-seed KV is preloaded with allocator pages and capacity charged but no paid import; controllers start clean with no in-flight writes (the paper does not publish its initial state). Every fresh request pays its native PD import.

Continuous batching: freed slots refill at the next step from the pre-imported requests of their own EP group (1 group(s), up to 2 per group, 2 in total; pool sized from the slots a group frees per step and the steps one import spans at Table I write rates, x4 margin; its KV counts against capacity); final-prompt queries join mixed decode cohorts.

Native layer runs on independent copies of the first continuous-refill boundary are physical; the stationary step, PD-import extra, refill schedule, cohorts and visible Tokens are separate conditional predictions.

Unsampled layers take their class's sampled step: the DRAM row openings that differ between same-class layers because their buffer addresses straddle row boundaries differently are assumed negligible and are not bounded; representative-point full native runs check every unsampled layer against its class interval.
Each point's independent error budget retains the 10% target; conditional budgets are not full-window detailed validation or silicon/paper accuracy guarantees.

Native NAND page service with OCP HBF v0.7 control and Table I geometry and timing; the host owns KV placement and block opens and there is no FTL or GC. Block size and erase time are research assumptions; every plane erasing at once is not stated by OCP.

NAND-backed KV: the host starts an import as a slot frees, fixes the step it joins and picks the free block that keeps its tail off the other tails' banks, knowing no request's length; reads and writes follow the block's address. The pick costs no time. Blocks mix requests of unequal lifetimes in real use, which holds extra NAND but moves no data.
8x40MB intermediate SRAM is modeled as a 320MB pool split across 128 die-local channel ports; aggregate bandwidth/latency/credits are explicit research inputs.
External Prefill producer source uses native DDR5 service geometry expanded to at least world x 100 GB/s; PD links and target KV writes remain the intended bottlenecks (research assumption).

PD import (user approved 2026-10-24): one stream per target rank, all streams concurrent; each import owns a 64 MiB source buffer cut into 1 MiB chunk slots dealt round-robin to its streams; a chunk holds its slot from source read until its target write completes (RDMA source-buffer semantics), so a stream keeps at most its slot count in flight while adjacent chunks' reads, links and writes overlap on the native timelines.
External producer streams prompt-1 KV tokens; native one-token final-prompt generates the first visible output and pays its complete cost.
Warmup seeds use real age-extended prompt histories and shorter remaining outputs to stagger completion; fresh measured requests retain the declared paper lengths.

Warmup-seed KV is preloaded with allocator pages and capacity charged but no paid import; controllers start clean with no in-flight writes (the paper does not publish its initial state). Every fresh request pays its native PD import.

Continuous batching: freed slots refill at the next step from the pre-imported requests of their own EP group (8 group(s), up to 2 per group, 16 in total; pool sized from the slots a group frees per step and the steps one import spans at Table I write rates, x4 margin; its KV counts against capacity); final-prompt queries join mixed decode cohorts.

Attention data parallelism over 8 EP groups: each group owns B/ep requests and runs their attention, dense MLP, router and shared expert on its own TP ranks (dense weights replicated per group, KV only on the owner group); MoE experts are shared by native all_to_all dispatch and combine across groups, and every layer ends at one cross-group barrier.

Native layer runs on independent copies of the first continuous-refill boundary are physical; the stationary step, PD-import extra, refill schedule, cohorts and visible Tokens are separate conditional predictions.

Unsampled layers take their class's sampled step: the DRAM row openings that differ between same-class layers because their buffer addresses straddle row boundaries differently are assumed negligible and are not bounded; representative-point full native runs check every unsampled layer against its class interval.
Each point's independent error budget retains the 10% target; conditional budgets are not full-window detailed validation or silicon/paper accuracy guarantees.

NAND-backed KV: the host starts an import as a slot frees, fixes the step it joins and picks the free block that keeps its tail off the other tails' banks, knowing no request's length; reads and writes follow the block's address. The pick costs no time. Blocks mix requests of unequal lifetimes in real use, which holds extra NAND but moves no data.
8x40MB intermediate SRAM is modeled as a 320MB pool split across 128 die-local channel ports; aggregate bandwidth/latency/credits are explicit research inputs.
External Prefill producer source uses native DDR5 service geometry expanded to at least world x 100 GB/s; PD links and target KV writes remain the intended bottlenecks (research assumption).

PD import (user approved 2026-10-24): one stream per target rank, all streams concurrent; each import owns a 64 MiB source buffer cut into 1 MiB chunk slots dealt round-robin to its streams; a chunk holds its slot from source read until its target write completes (RDMA source-buffer semantics), so a stream keeps at most its slot count in flight while adjacent chunks' reads, links and writes overlap on the native timelines.
External producer streams prompt-1 KV tokens; native one-token final-prompt generates the first visible output and pays its complete cost.
Warmup seeds use real age-extended prompt histories and shorter remaining outputs to stagger completion; fresh measured requests retain the declared paper lengths.

Attention data parallelism over 8 EP groups: each group owns B/ep requests and runs their attention, dense MLP, router and shared expert on its own TP ranks (dense weights replicated per group, KV only on the owner group); MoE experts are shared by native all_to_all dispatch and combine across groups, and every layer ends at one cross-group barrier.

Native serving, planner, GPU cost profiles and physical DRAM/NAND/SRAM services; no paper_* execution.
Paper Table I per-GPU capacity and interface budgets, BF16 model and KV, decimal workload K.

Native NAND page service with OCP HBF v0.7 control and Table I geometry and timing; the host owns KV placement and block opens and there is no FTL or GC. Block size and erase time are research assumptions; every plane erasing at once is not stated by OCP.

NAND-backed KV: the host starts an import as a slot frees, fixes the step it joins and picks the free block that keeps its tail off the other tails' banks, knowing no request's length; reads and writes follow the block's address. The pick costs no time. Blocks mix requests of unequal lifetimes in real use, which holds extra NAND but moves no data.
8x40MB intermediate SRAM is modeled as a 320MB pool split across 128 die-local channel ports; aggregate bandwidth/latency/credits are explicit research inputs.
External Prefill producer source uses native DDR5 service geometry expanded to at least world x 100 GB/s; PD links and target KV writes remain the intended bottlenecks (research assumption).

PD import (user approved 2026-10-24): one stream per target rank, all streams concurrent; each import owns a 64 MiB source buffer cut into 1 MiB chunk slots dealt round-robin to its streams; a chunk holds its slot from source read until its target write completes (RDMA source-buffer semantics), so a stream keeps at most its slot count in flight while adjacent chunks' reads, links and writes overlap on the native timelines.
External producer streams prompt-1 KV tokens; native one-token final-prompt generates the first visible output and pays its complete cost.
Warmup seeds use real age-extended prompt histories and shorter remaining outputs to stagger completion; fresh measured requests retain the declared paper lengths.

Warmup-seed KV is preloaded with allocator pages and capacity charged but no paid import; controllers start clean with no in-flight writes (the paper does not publish its initial state). Every fresh request pays its native PD import.

Continuous batching: freed slots refill at the next step from the pre-imported requests of their own EP group (4 group(s), up to 8 per group, 32 in total; pool sized from the slots a group frees per step and the steps one import spans at Table I write rates, x4 margin; its KV counts against capacity); final-prompt queries join mixed decode cohorts.

Attention data parallelism over 4 EP groups: each group owns B/ep requests and runs their attention, dense MLP, router and shared expert on its own TP ranks (dense weights replicated per group, KV only on the owner group); MoE experts are shared by native all_to_all dispatch and combine across groups, and every layer ends at one cross-group barrier.

Native layer runs on independent copies of the first continuous-refill boundary are physical; the stationary step, PD-import extra, refill schedule, cohorts and visible Tokens are separate conditional predictions.

Unsampled layers take their class's sampled step: the DRAM row openings that differ between same-class layers because their buffer addresses straddle row boundaries differently are assumed negligible and are not bounded; representative-point full native runs check every unsampled layer against its class interval.
Each point's independent error budget retains the 10% target; conditional budgets are not full-window detailed validation or silicon/paper accuracy guarantees.

assumptions: Unsampled layers take their class's sampled step: the DRAM row openings that differ between same-class layers because their buffer addresses straddle row boundaries differently are assumed negligible and are not bounded; representative-point full native runs check every unsampled layer against its class interval.

Native serving, planner, GPU cost profiles and physical DRAM/NAND/SRAM services; no paper_* execution.
Paper Table I per-GPU capacity and interface budgets, BF16 model and KV, decimal workload K.

Native NAND page service with OCP HBF v0.7 control and Table I geometry and timing; the host owns KV placement and block opens and there is no FTL or GC. Block size and erase time are research assumptions; every plane erasing at once is not stated by OCP.

NAND-backed KV: the host starts an import as a slot frees, fixes the step it joins and picks the free block that keeps its tail off the other tails' banks, knowing no request's length; reads and writes follow the block's address. The pick costs no time. Blocks mix requests of unequal lifetimes in real use, which holds extra NAND but moves no data.
8x40MB intermediate SRAM is modeled as a 320MB pool split across 128 die-local channel ports; aggregate bandwidth/latency/credits are explicit research inputs.
External Prefill producer source uses native DDR5 service geometry expanded to at least world x 100 GB/s; PD links and target KV writes remain the intended bottlenecks (research assumption).

PD import (user approved 2026-10-24): one stream per target rank, all streams concurrent; each import owns a 64 MiB source buffer cut into 1 MiB chunk slots dealt round-robin to its streams; a chunk holds its slot from source read until its target write completes (RDMA source-buffer semantics), so a stream keeps at most its slot count in flight while adjacent chunks' reads, links and writes overlap on the native timelines.
External producer streams prompt-1 KV tokens; native one-token final-prompt generates the first visible output and pays its complete cost.
Warmup seeds use real age-extended prompt histories and shorter remaining outputs to stagger completion; fresh measured requests retain the declared paper lengths.

Warmup-seed KV is preloaded with allocator pages and capacity charged but no paid import; controllers start clean with no in-flight writes (the paper does not publish its initial state). Every fresh request pays its native PD import.

Continuous batching: freed slots refill at the next step from the pre-imported requests of their own EP group (2 group(s), up to 6 per group, 12 in total; pool sized from the slots a group frees per step and the steps one import spans at Table I write rates, x4 margin; its KV counts against capacity); final-prompt queries join mixed decode cohorts.

Attention data parallelism over 2 EP groups: each group owns B/ep requests and runs their attention, dense MLP, router and shared expert on its own TP ranks (dense weights replicated per group, KV only on the owner group); MoE experts are shared by native all_to_all dispatch and combine across groups, and every layer ends at one cross-group barrier.

Native layer runs on independent copies of the first continuous-refill boundary are physical; the stationary step, PD-import extra, refill schedule, cohorts and visible Tokens are separate conditional predictions.

Unsampled layers take their class's sampled step: the DRAM row openings that differ between same-class layers because their buffer addresses straddle row boundaries differently are assumed negligible and are not bounded; representative-point full native runs check every unsampled layer against its class interval.
Each point's independent error budget retains the 10% target; conditional budgets are not full-window detailed validation or silicon/paper accuracy guarantees.

Native serving, planner, GPU cost profiles and physical DRAM/NAND/SRAM services; no paper_* execution.
Paper Table I per-GPU capacity and interface budgets, BF16 model and KV, decimal workload K.

Native NAND page service with OCP HBF v0.7 control and Table I geometry and timing; the host owns KV placement and block opens and there is no FTL or GC. Block size and erase time are research assumptions; every plane erasing at once is not stated by OCP.

NAND-backed KV: the host starts an import as a slot frees, fixes the step it joins and picks the free block that keeps its tail off the other tails' banks, knowing no request's length; reads and writes follow the block's address. The pick costs no time. Blocks mix requests of unequal lifetimes in real use, which holds extra NAND but moves no data.
8x40MB intermediate SRAM is modeled as a 320MB pool split across 128 die-local channel ports; aggregate bandwidth/latency/credits are explicit research inputs.
External Prefill producer source uses native DDR5 service geometry expanded to at least world x 100 GB/s; PD links and target KV writes remain the intended bottlenecks (research assumption).

PD import (user approved 2026-10-24): one stream per target rank, all streams concurrent; each import owns a 64 MiB source buffer cut into 1 MiB chunk slots dealt round-robin to its streams; a chunk holds its slot from source read until its target write completes (RDMA source-buffer semantics), so a stream keeps at most its slot count in flight while adjacent chunks' reads, links and writes overlap on the native timelines.
External producer streams prompt-1 KV tokens; native one-token final-prompt generates the first visible output and pays its complete cost.
Warmup seeds use real age-extended prompt histories and shorter remaining outputs to stagger completion; fresh measured requests retain the declared paper lengths.

Warmup-seed KV is preloaded with allocator pages and capacity charged but no paid import; controllers start clean with no in-flight writes (the paper does not publish its initial state). Every fresh request pays its native PD import.

Continuous batching: freed slots refill at the next step from the pre-imported requests of their own EP group (1 group(s), up to 4 per group, 4 in total; pool sized from the slots a group frees per step and the steps one import spans at Table I write rates, x4 margin; its KV counts against capacity); final-prompt queries join mixed decode cohorts.

Native layer runs on independent copies of the first continuous-refill boundary are physical; the stationary step, PD-import extra, refill schedule, cohorts and visible Tokens are separate conditional predictions.

Unsampled layers take their class's sampled step: the DRAM row openings that differ between same-class layers because their buffer addresses straddle row boundaries differently are assumed negligible and are not bounded; representative-point full native runs check every unsampled layer against its class interval.
Each point's independent error budget retains the 10% target; conditional budgets are not full-window detailed validation or silicon/paper accuracy guarantees.

Native serving, planner, GPU cost profiles and physical DRAM/NAND/SRAM services; no paper_* execution.
Paper Table I per-GPU capacity and interface budgets, BF16 model and KV, decimal workload K.

Native NAND page service with OCP HBF v0.7 control and Table I geometry and timing; the host owns KV placement and block opens and there is no FTL or GC. Block size and erase time are research assumptions; every plane erasing at once is not stated by OCP.

NAND-backed KV: the host starts an import as a slot frees, fixes the step it joins and picks the free block that keeps its tail off the other tails' banks, knowing no request's length; reads and writes follow the block's address. The pick costs no time. Blocks mix requests of unequal lifetimes in real use, which holds extra NAND but moves no data.
8x40MB intermediate SRAM is modeled as a 320MB pool split across 128 die-local channel ports; aggregate bandwidth/latency/credits are explicit research inputs.
External Prefill producer source uses native DDR5 service geometry expanded to at least world x 100 GB/s; PD links and target KV writes remain the intended bottlenecks (research assumption).

PD import (user approved 2026-10-24): one stream per target rank, all streams concurrent; each import owns a 64 MiB source buffer cut into 1 MiB chunk slots dealt round-robin to its streams; a chunk holds its slot from source read until its target write completes (RDMA source-buffer semantics), so a stream keeps at most its slot count in flight while adjacent chunks' reads, links and writes overlap on the native timelines.
External producer streams prompt-1 KV tokens; native one-token final-prompt generates the first visible output and pays its complete cost.
Warmup seeds use real age-extended prompt histories and shorter remaining outputs to stagger completion; fresh measured requests retain the declared paper lengths.

Warmup-seed KV is preloaded with allocator pages and capacity charged but no paid import; controllers start clean with no in-flight writes (the paper does not publish its initial state). Every fresh request pays its native PD import.

Continuous batching: freed slots refill at the next step from the pre-imported requests of their own EP group (2 group(s), up to 2 per group, 4 in total; pool sized from the slots a group frees per step and the steps one import spans at Table I write rates, x4 margin; its KV counts against capacity); final-prompt queries join mixed decode cohorts.

Attention data parallelism over 2 EP groups: each group owns B/ep requests and runs their attention, dense MLP, router and shared expert on its own TP ranks (dense weights replicated per group, KV only on the owner group); MoE experts are shared by native all_to_all dispatch and combine across groups, and every layer ends at one cross-group barrier.

Native layer runs on independent copies of the first continuous-refill boundary are physical; the stationary step, PD-import extra, refill schedule, cohorts and visible Tokens are separate conditional predictions.

Unsampled layers take their class's sampled step: the DRAM row openings that differ between same-class layers because their buffer addresses straddle row boundaries differently are assumed negligible and are not bounded; representative-point full native runs check every unsampled layer against its class interval.
Each point's independent error budget retains the 10% target; conditional budgets are not full-window detailed validation or silicon/paper accuracy guarantees.

assumptions: Unsampled layers take their class's sampled step: the DRAM row openings that differ between same-class layers because their buffer addresses straddle row boundaries differently are assumed negligible and are not bounded; representative-point full native runs check every unsampled layer against its class interval.

Native serving, planner, GPU cost profiles and physical DRAM/NAND/SRAM services; no paper_* execution.
Paper Table I per-GPU capacity and interface budgets, BF16 model and KV, decimal workload K.

Native NAND page service with OCP HBF v0.7 control and Table I geometry and timing; the host owns KV placement and block opens and there is no FTL or GC. Block size and erase time are research assumptions; every plane erasing at once is not stated by OCP.

NAND-backed KV: the host starts an import as a slot frees, fixes the step it joins and picks the free block that keeps its tail off the other tails' banks, knowing no request's length; reads and writes follow the block's address. The pick costs no time. Blocks mix requests of unequal lifetimes in real use, which holds extra NAND but moves no data.
8x40MB intermediate SRAM is modeled as a 320MB pool split across 128 die-local channel ports; aggregate bandwidth/latency/credits are explicit research inputs.
External Prefill producer source uses native DDR5 service geometry expanded to at least world x 100 GB/s; PD links and target KV writes remain the intended bottlenecks (research assumption).

PD import (user approved 2026-10-24): one stream per target rank, all streams concurrent; each import owns a 64 MiB source buffer cut into 1 MiB chunk slots dealt round-robin to its streams; a chunk holds its slot from source read until its target write completes (RDMA source-buffer semantics), so a stream keeps at most its slot count in flight while adjacent chunks' reads, links and writes overlap on the native timelines.
External producer streams prompt-1 KV tokens; native one-token final-prompt generates the first visible output and pays its complete cost.
Warmup seeds use real age-extended prompt histories and shorter remaining outputs to stagger completion; fresh measured requests retain the declared paper lengths.

Warmup-seed KV is preloaded with allocator pages and capacity charged but no paid import; controllers start clean with no in-flight writes (the paper does not publish its initial state). Every fresh request pays its native PD import.

Continuous batching: freed slots refill at the next step from the pre-imported requests of their own EP group (4 group(s), up to 2 per group, 8 in total; pool sized from the slots a group frees per step and the steps one import spans at Table I write rates, x4 margin; its KV counts against capacity); final-prompt queries join mixed decode cohorts.

Attention data parallelism over 4 EP groups: each group owns B/ep requests and runs their attention, dense MLP, router and shared expert on its own TP ranks (dense weights replicated per group, KV only on the owner group); MoE experts are shared by native all_to_all dispatch and combine across groups, and every layer ends at one cross-group barrier.

Native layer runs on independent copies of the first continuous-refill boundary are physical; the stationary step, PD-import extra, refill schedule, cohorts and visible Tokens are separate conditional predictions.

Unsampled layers take their class's sampled step: the DRAM row openings that differ between same-class layers because their buffer addresses straddle row boundaries differently are assumed negligible and are not bounded; representative-point full native runs check every unsampled layer against its class interval.
Each point's independent error budget retains the 10% target; conditional budgets are not full-window detailed validation or silicon/paper accuracy guarantees.

NAND-backed KV: the host starts an import as a slot frees, fixes the step it joins and picks the free block that keeps its tail off the other tails' banks, knowing no request's length; reads and writes follow the block's address. Native serving, planner, GPU cost profiles and physical DRAM/NAND/SRAM services; no paper_* execution.
Paper Table I per-GPU capacity and interface budgets, BF16 model and KV, decimal workload K.

Native NAND page service with OCP HBF v0.7 control and Table I geometry and timing; the host owns KV placement and block opens and there is no FTL or GC. Block size and erase time are research assumptions; every plane erasing at once is not stated by OCP.

NAND-backed KV: the host starts an import as a slot frees, fixes the step it joins and picks the free block that keeps its tail off the other tails' banks, knowing no request's length; reads and writes follow the block's address. The pick costs no time. Blocks mix requests of unequal lifetimes in real use, which holds extra NAND but moves no data.
8x40MB intermediate SRAM is modeled as a 320MB pool split across 128 die-local channel ports; aggregate bandwidth/latency/credits are explicit research inputs.
External Prefill producer source uses native DDR5 service geometry expanded to at least world x 100 GB/s; PD links and target KV writes remain the intended bottlenecks (research assumption).

PD import (user approved 2026-10-24): one stream per target rank, all streams concurrent; each import owns a 64 MiB source buffer cut into 1 MiB chunk slots dealt round-robin to its streams; a chunk holds its slot from source read until its target write completes (RDMA source-buffer semantics), so a stream keeps at most its slot count in flight while adjacent chunks' reads, links and writes overlap on the native timelines.
External producer streams prompt-1 KV tokens; native one-token final-prompt generates the first visible output and pays its complete cost.
Warmup seeds use real age-extended prompt histories and shorter remaining outputs to stagger completion; fresh measured requests retain the declared paper lengths.

Warmup-seed KV is preloaded with allocator pages and capacity charged but no paid import; controllers start clean with no in-flight writes (the paper does not publish its initial state). Every fresh request pays its native PD import.

Continuous batching: freed slots refill at the next step from the pre-imported requests of their own EP group (8 group(s), up to 4 per group, 32 in total; pool sized from the slots a group frees per step and the steps one import spans at Table I write rates, x4 margin; its KV counts against capacity); final-prompt queries join mixed decode cohorts.

Attention data parallelism over 8 EP groups: each group owns B/ep requests and runs their attention, dense MLP, router and shared expert on its own TP ranks (dense weights replicated per group, KV only on the owner group); MoE experts are shared by native all_to_all dispatch and combine across groups, and every layer ends at one cross-group barrier.

Native layer runs on independent copies of the first continuous-refill boundary are physical; the stationary step, PD-import extra, refill schedule, cohorts and visible Tokens are separate conditional predictions.

Unsampled layers take their class's sampled step: the DRAM row openings that differ between same-class layers because their buffer addresses straddle row boundaries differently are assumed negligible and are not bounded; representative-point full native runs check every unsampled layer against its class interval.
Each point's independent error budget retains the 10% target; conditional budgets are not full-window detailed validation or silicon/paper accuracy guarantees.

NAND-backed KV: the host starts an import as a slot frees, fixes the step it joins and picks the free block that keeps its tail off the other tails' banks, knowing no request's length; reads and writes follow the block's address. The pick costs no time. Blocks mix requests of unequal lifetimes in real use, which holds extra NAND but moves no data.
8x40MB intermediate SRAM is modeled as a 320MB pool split across 128 die-local channel ports; aggregate bandwidth/latency/credits are explicit research inputs.
External Prefill producer source uses native DDR5 service geometry expanded to at least world x 100 GB/s; PD links and target KV writes remain the intended bottlenecks (research assumption).

PD import (user approved 2026-10-24): one stream per target rank, all streams concurrent; each import owns a 64 MiB source buffer cut into 1 MiB chunk slots dealt round-robin to its streams; a chunk holds its slot from source read until its target write completes (RDMA source-buffer semantics), so a stream keeps at most its slot count in flight while adjacent chunks' reads, links and writes overlap on the native timelines.
